---
title: "05_analysis_1"
format: html
---

## Aim

Which genes in the baseline biopsy differ between lesions that later
persisted or progressed (Groups 1 + 3) and lesions that regressed or stayed
normal (Groups 2 + 4)? 

For every gene we fit two linear models:

- Unadjusted: `log2_expr ~ outcome`
- Adjusted: `log2_expr ~ outcome + baseline_frozen`

The adjusted model asks whether a gene carries information about the
future course of the lesion beyond how abnormal the tissue already was at
baseline (persistent lesions were more often dysplastic at baseline, and the
PCA in `04_describe` shows that expression follows histological grade).

## Load libraries and data

```{r}
library("here")
library("broom")
library("tidyverse")

# The RStudio Server has no display: draw PNG files without X11
options(bitmapType = "cairo")

dat_aug <- read_tsv(
  here("data/03_augmented_data.tsv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

expr_clean <- read_tsv(
  here("data/02_clean_expression.tsv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

## Define the outcome

Groups 1 and 3 became (or stayed) dysplastic at follow-up: persistent.
Groups 2 and 4 were non-dysplastic at follow-up: regressive.
"regressive" is the reference level, so a positive estimate means "higher in
persistent lesions".

```{r}
dat_aug <- dat_aug |>
  mutate(
    outcome = case_when(
      outcome_group %in% c("Group 1", "Group 3") ~ "persistent",
      outcome_group %in% c("Group 2", "Group 4") ~ "regressive"
    ),
    outcome = factor(outcome, levels = c("regressive", "persistent"))
  )

# Check: 32 persistent and 31 regressive biopsies
dat_aug |>
  count(outcome_group, outcome)
```

## Gene symbol lookup

`03_augment` names the gene columns by Entrez ID only. The symbols are taken
from `02_clean_expression.tsv`, which holds both identifiers.

```{r}
gene_lookup <- expr_clean |>
  dplyr::select(ENTREZ_ID, SYMBOL) |>
  dplyr::rename(entrez_id = ENTREZ_ID, symbol = SYMBOL) |>
  mutate(entrez_id = as.character(entrez_id))
```

## From wide to long format

One row per biopsy and gene. Gene columns are the columns whose name is a
number (Entrez ID).

```{r}
dat_long <- dat_aug |>
  dplyr::select(
    sample_id,
    outcome_group,
    outcome,
    baseline_frozen,
    matches("^[0-9]+$")
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^[0-9]+$"),
    names_to = "entrez_id",
    values_to = "log2_expr"
  ) |>
  left_join(gene_lookup, by = "entrez_id")

# Check: rows = 63 biopsies x number of genes, and every gene has a symbol
dat_long |>
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_samples = n_distinct(sample_id),
    n_genes = n_distinct(entrez_id),
    n_missing_symbol = sum(is.na(symbol))
  )
```

## Fit two linear models per gene

Nest the data per gene, then fit both models with `map()`. We tidy each
model straight away (`broom::tidy()`) instead of keeping ~40,000 full model
objects, which would use a lot of memory.

```{r}
dat_nested <- dat_long |>
  group_by(entrez_id, symbol) |>
  nest() |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    tidy_unadjusted = map(
      .x = data,
      .f = ~ lm(log2_expr ~ outcome, data = .x) |>
        tidy(conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
    ),
    tidy_adjusted = map(
      .x = data,
      .f = ~ lm(log2_expr ~ outcome + baseline_frozen, data = .x) |>
        tidy(conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
    )
  )
```

## Collect the outcome estimates and correct for multiple testing

For each model we keep the `outcomepersistent` term: the difference in mean
log2 expression between persistent and regressive lesions (log2 fold
change). P-values are corrected per model with Benjamini-Hochberg (false
discovery rate), as in the original paper (FDR ≤ 0.05).

```{r}
de_results <- dat_nested |>
  dplyr::select(entrez_id, symbol, tidy_unadjusted, tidy_adjusted) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(tidy_unadjusted, tidy_adjusted),
    names_to = "model",
    names_prefix = "tidy_",
    values_to = "model_tidy"
  ) |>
  unnest(model_tidy) |>
  filter(term == "outcomepersistent") |>
  dplyr::select(-term) |>
  group_by(model) |>
  mutate(q_value = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    is_significant = q_value <= 0.05,
    direction = case_when(
      is_significant & estimate > 0 ~ "Higher in persistent",
      is_significant & estimate < 0 ~ "Higher in regressive",
      .default = "Not significant"
    )
  )
```

## Key numbers

```{r}
key_numbers <- de_results |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(
    n_genes_tested = n(),
    n_significant = sum(is_significant),
    n_higher_persistent = sum(direction == "Higher in persistent"),
    n_higher_regressive = sum(direction == "Higher in regressive")
  )

key_numbers
```

## Genes highlighted in the paper

The paper reports PLK1 (cell cycle), DSG3 and JUP (cell adhesion) as higher
in persistent lesions.

```{r}
key_genes <- c("PLK1", "DSG3", "JUP")

de_results |>
  filter(symbol %in% key_genes) |>
  dplyr::select(symbol, model, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value, q_value) |>
  arrange(symbol, model)
```

## Plot 1: volcano plot (unadjusted model)

```{r}
volcano_plot <- de_results |>
  filter(model == "unadjusted") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = -log10(p.value), colour = direction)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  geom_label(
    data = de_results |>
      filter(model == "unadjusted", symbol %in% key_genes),
    aes(label = symbol),
    colour = "black",
    size = 3,
    nudge_y = 0.4
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Higher in persistent" = "firebrick",
      "Higher in regressive" = "steelblue",
      "Not significant" = "grey70"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Persistent vs regressive bronchial lesions",
    x = "log2 fold change (persistent - regressive)",
    y = "-log10(p-value)",
    colour = "FDR <= 0.05"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

volcano_plot
```

## Plot 2: forest plot of the top 20 genes (unadjusted model)

```{r}
forest_plot <- de_results |>
  filter(model == "unadjusted", is_significant) |>
  slice_min(q_value, n = 20) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = estimate,
    y = fct_reorder(symbol, estimate),
    xmin = conf.low,
    xmax = conf.high,
    colour = direction
  )) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_errorbarh(height = 0.3) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Higher in persistent" = "firebrick",
      "Higher in regressive" = "steelblue"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 20 genes by FDR",
    x = "log2 fold change with 95% CI",
    y = NULL,
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

forest_plot
```

## Plot 3: does the effect survive adjustment for baseline grade?

One point per gene. Points on the diagonal keep their effect after
adjustment; points that move towards zero mainly reflect baseline severity.

```{r}
adjustment_comparison <- de_results |>
  dplyr::select(entrez_id, symbol, model, estimate, is_significant) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = model,
    values_from = c(estimate, is_significant)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    significance = case_when(
      is_significant_unadjusted & is_significant_adjusted ~ "Both models",
      is_significant_unadjusted ~ "Unadjusted only",
      is_significant_adjusted ~ "Adjusted only",
      .default = "Neither"
    )
  )

adjustment_comparison |>
  count(significance)

adjustment_plot <- adjustment_comparison |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = estimate_unadjusted,
    y = estimate_adjusted,
    colour = significance
  )) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Both models" = "darkorange",
      "Unadjusted only" = "steelblue",
      "Adjusted only" = "purple",
      "Neither" = "grey70"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Effect of adjusting for baseline histological grade",
    x = "log2 fold change, unadjusted",
    y = "log2 fold change, adjusted for baseline grade",
    colour = "Significant in"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

adjustment_plot
```

## Plot 4: the paper's key genes in the four outcome groups

```{r}
key_gene_plot <- dat_long |>
  filter(symbol %in% key_genes) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = outcome_group, y = log2_expr, fill = outcome)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ symbol, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Genes highlighted in the original paper",
    x = NULL,
    y = "log2 expression",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

key_gene_plot
```

## Save results and plots

```{r}
dir.create(here("results"), showWarnings = FALSE)

write_tsv(de_results, here("results/05_de_results.tsv"))
write_tsv(key_numbers, here("results/05_key_numbers.tsv"))

ggsave(
  here("results/05_volcano.png"),
  volcano_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
ggsave(
  here("results/05_forest_top20.png"),
  forest_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
ggsave(
  here("results/05_adjusted_vs_unadjusted.png"),
  adjustment_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
ggsave(
  here("results/05_key_genes.png"),
  key_gene_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 4,
  dpi = 300
)
```
